_comment: EA conformance cases where custos intentionally differs (see the rule spec's Divergences section). Keys: '<test>#<method>/<fixture basename>' as printed by TestEA; values: reason.
src/test/java/com/kalessil/phpStorm/phpI: fix emits PHPUnit's real method names (assertFileDoesNotExist / assertDirectoryDoesNotExist) instead of upstream's misspelled ones
upstream's IDE formatter re-spaces an unreported `array& $arr` parameter; custos edits only the reported ranges

upstream's IDE formatter re-spaces an untouched inner for header (custos copies the body verbatim); additionally a limit variable reused by several loops is resolved from the assignment reaching each loop (one extra report); loops whose counter or header-assigned limit is mentioned after the loop are not reported (two fewer reports)

fixes keep named arguments: a named flags: value is extended with JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR (upstream leaves it unfixed) and the result-type fix appends associative: by name instead of rebuilding the call positionally and dropping flags:
below PHP 8.0 no fix when the array may have string keys (unpacking would throw)
loose ==/!= forms are not reported: they ignore key order and are not equivalent to array_is_list()
array-typed arguments are spread via ...array_values() so string keys neither throw (<8.1) nor collide (>=8.1)
get_parent_class() in a class without extends is not rewritten to parent::class (fatal error)
get_class() outside a class is not rewritten to __CLASS__ (empty there); version_compare(..., '7.1', '==') not rewritten (patch level makes it non-equivalent)
reported without a fix: get_debug_type() names differ from gettype() for scalars (int/integer, float/double, null/NULL)

only exact equivalents get a fix (is_a, get_class on a final class, class_implements with an interface literal on an object); get_parent_class/is_subclass_of/class_parents and non-final get_class are reported without a fix
the or-form re-check emits || is_dir($concurrentDirectory) (upstream negates it, inverting the logic)
below PHPUnit 9.1 the fix suggests assertFileNotExists/assertDirectoryNotExists (the DoesNotExist names do not exist yet)
no fix below PHP 7.0 (?? does not parse); ?? '' guard from 7.0; negative offsets other than -1 skipped (strlen($s) - n can go negative)

4-argument mb_substr fix emits mb_strpos($h, $n, 0, $enc); case-folded comparisons only against literals already in folded case; loose ==/!= comparisons get a fix only against non-numeric string literals
calls with call-time & arguments are not reported/rewritten ($fn($a, &$b) is a fatal error since PHP 5.4)
an override that calls the parent without return, where the parent returns a value, is not reported (removing it would change return values)
the generated limit variable avoids names already used in the scope ($iMax1 instead of overwriting $iMax)
assertInternalType is reported only when the declared return type always satisfies the named type; unknown/contradicting type names are not reported (that call fails, it is not redundant)
method/static calls are not reordered (they may have side effects); isset($x[...]) && $x is not reported (isset also guards $x itself)
under && the broader (redundant) instanceof is reported, not the more specific one
an own property incompatible with the trait's (different default, visibility, static, readonly or type) is reported as an error: PHP refuses to compose such a class
keys are compared as PHP stores them (escapes decoded, '7' == 7, any integer base); duplicate integer keys are reported too
for a bool operand the fix emits x() instead of false !== x()
no suggestion when the declaration would be a compile error (": void" with return $x where $x is null/void-documented, "?T" with a bare return)
a private untyped property without default (and not assigned by the constructor) holds null until written, so a cast of it is not redundant even when its @var names the target type
a private untyped property without default (and not assigned by the constructor) holds null until written, so a cast of it is not redundant even when its @var names the target type

string-API rewrites only when equivalent: `^T$` without the D modifier also matches T followed by a newline (no identity-comparison rewrite), and `\s` trims are spelled with PCRE's exact character set; preg_replace() is rewritten to str_replace() only when the replacement is a literal free of backslashes and `$` (or a number/int cast): preg_replace() interprets back-references and `\\` in it
`^T$` without the D modifier also matches T followed by a newline, so no identity-comparison rewrite is offered
closures and arrow functions defined in a method of the declaring class are checked like the method (they have its class scope); upstream reports them unconditionally

success tests of include_once/require_once (conditions, logical operands, comparison with false) are not reported, and there is no quick-fix: a plain include/require re-runs the file and redeclares its symbols

no null-comparison suggestion for int/float/bool|null subjects (empty() is also true for 0, 0.0, false) nor for possibly unassigned variables (`=== null` warns); such subjects get the generic report; fixes only when native declarations alone give the same types (PHPDoc-only types are reported without a fix)

no rename fix for single-underscore magic names: renaming breaks callers and the signature may not fit the magic contract (e.g. one-parameter _set -> fatal __set); single-underscore methods that are deliberate hooks (the class also declares the magic counterpart, or the file calls the method by name) are not reported
fix uses static:: (keeps late static binding); self:: only for private/final methods or final classes/enums
kind S strict fix only when the other operand is known to be string/null/array (int/float from PHP 8.0); untyped operands get no fix
no fix for literals with a leading backslash: X::class has none, so the string value would change
no fix for literals with a leading backslash: X::class has none, so the string value would change
a parameter without a declared or documented type accepts any value: its default value is not treated as its type (one fewer report)

in_array() over array_keys() is reported without a fix unless array_key_exists() is equivalent: '5' is stored as the int key 5 and loose comparison matches numeric strings, so only int-typed needles (strict) and non-numeric string literals qualify
reported without a fix: adding true changes the result whenever loose and strict equality differ ('1' == 1, null == ''); the equivalent cases are already exempt
a parent magic method with an empty body (and no promoted constructor parameter) does nothing, so not calling it is not reported
a parent magic method with an empty body (and no promoted constructor parameter) does nothing, so not calling it is not reported
realpath() drops trailing separators: `__DIR__ . '/../'` becomes dirname(__DIR__) without a `. '/'` tail
an imported short name or alias written in another case is not reported: ::class yields the import's target as written in the use statement, which is correct when the import is
a plain literal made only of letters, digits, whitespace, backslashes and characters preg_quote() escapes cannot yield an unescaped delimiter: not reported
a format held in an instance property that a subclass may redeclare (non-private, class not final) is not resolved: the subclass default would be used
statements that output (echo, print, printf) are per-iteration by nature and not reported: moving them out of the loop changes the output

the fix is offered only when the case-insensitive search is equivalent (both sides converted the same way, or the other side a literal without letters of the opposite case); otherwise reported without a fix
Unicode escapes are looked for in the decoded pattern: a single-quoted '/\\p/' is the pattern \p (reported), while '/A\\\P/' is an escaped backslash followed by P (not reported)

self::m() / Foo::m() are rewritten to $this->m() only when no subclass can override m (private or final method, final class or enum, no indexed descendant declaring it) and the name resolves to the called method: otherwise reported without a fix, since $this->m() would run the override
keyed array values are not reported at file level either (`return ['postflight' => function () {...}]` is bound by the including code)
